identity.title: MOS: Model Synergy for Test-Time Adaptation on LiDAR-Based 3D Object Detection

problem.claim: Online test-time adaptation for LiDAR-based 3D object detectors under domain shifts, including simultaneous cross-dataset shifts and sensor/weather corruptions.

gap.claim: Practical sensor and weather corruptions are described as underexplored relative to cross-dataset shifts, especially when both shift types co-occur.

contributions.claim: MOS dynamically selects historical checkpoints with diverse knowledge and assembles them using Synergy Weights for the current test batch.
Synergy Weights use predicted-box similarity and feature independence to guide checkpoint weighting, while low-scoring checkpoints are replaced by newly updated models.
The study evaluates adaptation across three datasets and eight corruption types, including a cross-corruption setting.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present MOS as a novel online test-time adaptation framework that uses long-term knowledge from prior test batches and targets cross-corruption shifts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MOS outperformed existing test-time adaptation strategies across three datasets and eight corruption types.
The authors report a 67.3% improvement in the cross-corruption scenario.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deployment domain shifts degrade LiDAR-based 3D detection, while practical sensor and weather corruptions receive less attention.
The authors introduce online adaptation for diverse shifts, including co-occurring cross-dataset shifts and corruptions, and use prior test batches to mitigate catastrophic forgetting.
MOS selects diverse historical checkpoints and combines them through Synergy Weights based on prediction similarity and feature independence.
The model bank discards low-scoring checkpoints; experiments span three datasets and eight corruption types, with a reported 67.3% cross-corruption improvement.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links checkpoint selection to two explicit signals—predicted-box similarity and feature independence—and links model-bank replacement to average Synergy Weight scores.

lessons.interpretation: A method description becomes more actionable when each adaptive component is paired with its decision signal and update rule.
lessons.application: When presenting an adaptive system, specify the observable signals driving selection, aggregation, and replacement, then state how each signal affects the component.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the decision process is intentionally learned end-to-end or cannot be meaningfully decomposed into interpretable signals.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metric, or experimental conditions behind the reported superiority.
The meaning and denominator of the 67.3% improvement are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide ablations separating long-term knowledge, checkpoint diversity, Synergy Weights, and model-bank replacement.
